answer: A useful defense is a stake-and-history bond: before an agent can join a shared market, it must lock a modest deposit and build a verifiable record of useful work over time, like a reef that grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight. A newcomer starts at dawn with a tiny trust limit; only consistent, checked contributions raise it, so a sybil flood faces a river of rising costs — each fake identity must pay the same deposit and wait through the same long history, making mass forgery unprofitable while honest agents earn their way in.
